slides.say: For every number t, diamond of t is equal to t squared. In the choices, x is zero or more. Which of the following is not always true?

Look at the choices. The diamond appears in every choice, two or three times. But each diamond here only squares something, so the work is short, and we solve it now. A tip for the exam: if a question would take a lot of calculating, you can skip it, solve the rest of the section, and come back at the end. Decide by the work it needs, not by how many symbols you see. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with algebra, and then by plugging in a number.

[short pause] With algebra, we write what the diamond does on each side. The diamond squares whatever goes in. Choice number one. On the left, six x goes in, so we get six x, squared. That's six squared times x squared, thirty-six x squared. On the right, thirty-six times x squared. Both sides are equal for every x, so this one is always true, and it's out.
Choice number two. Diamond of root x is root x, squared, which is x. So the left side is x times x, which is x squared. The right side is diamond of x, x squared too. Always true, so it's out.

Choice number three. On the left, five x, squared, is twenty-five x squared. On the right, five times x squared is only five x squared. These are equal only when x is zero. For any other x, they're different. So this one is not always true, and choice number three is our answer.
at: and choice number three is our answer

slides.say: In the exam you'd circle it and move on. But choice number four teaches something useful. x minus seven and seven minus x are opposites, and opposites have the same square. So the two sides are always equal.

[pause] Now let's plug in a number. It's usually faster, because we don't open anything. Let's take x is one, a small nonzero value. Zero is allowed too, but with zero, choice number three gives zero on both sides, so it can't show the failure. Choice number one. Diamond of six is thirty-six, and thirty-six times diamond of one is thirty-six times one, thirty-six. Equal. Choice number two. Diamond of one is one, and one times one is one. Diamond of one is one too. Equal.
at: Diamond of one is one too

slides.say: Choice number three. Diamond of five is twenty-five, but five times diamond of one is five times one, which is five. Twenty-five is not five, so choice number three fails.

One allowed example where a choice fails proves it's not always true, so we can stop here without checking choice number four. Choice number three is the one that broke. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
